context: The population of a small town grows at a constant average percentage rate each year.

params.why: the unrounded population must be a whole number, so the entry-level answer is exact

stem: The current population of a small town is ${=P}$ and the average rate of population growth is ${=r}$ % p.a. Use the compound interest formula to calculate what the town council can expect the population to be in ${=n}$ years' time.
solution: Write down the known values: $P={=P}$, $i=\frac{{=r}}{100}$, $n={=n}$ and $A=?$
Write down the compound interest formula: $A=P(1+i)^{n}$
The town council can expect the population to be ${=A}$ in ${=n}$ years' time.
notes: Entry point of the skill: one application of A = P(1+i)^n with n = 2 or 3. P is a multiple of 400 (n = 2) or 8000 (n = 3) and the rate is 5, 10, 20 or 25 %, so the result is always an exact whole number and no rounding is asked. Integrality is enforced by a require. 64 distinct instances. Model: worked example 11 (page 346): same known-values, formula, substitute, answer layout. The stem names the compound interest formula so a blind solver cannot read the growth as simple (linear) growth.
